== Formal definition ==

Let $\vec{u},\vec{v},\vec{w}$ be vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Is defined their '''scalar triple product'''

$$
\vec{u}\cdot(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})
$$
<ref>{{#cite:Q2329}}</ref><ref>{{#cite:Q2330}}</ref>

== Geometrical interpretation ==

The absolute value of the scalar triple product calculates the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by the three vectors.

[[File:Scalar-triple-product-parallelepiped.svg|thumb|center|560px|alt=Parallelepiped spanned by u, v and w, with the base parallelogram shaded and the three hidden edges dashed|The parallelepiped spanned by $\vec{u}$, $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$. The shaded base spanned by $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{w}$ has area $\lvert\vec{v}\times\vec{w}\rvert$; the height $h=\lvert\vec{u}\rvert\,\lvert\cos\varphi\rvert$ is dropped from the tip of $\vec{u}$ onto the base plane, and the three edges hidden behind the solid are dashed.]]

{{Hidden proof}}
Base area: $|\vec{v}\times\vec{w}|$

Height $h=|\vec{u}|\,|\cos\varphi|$, where $\varphi$ is the angle between $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}\times\vec{w}$,

$$
V=|\vec{v}\times\vec{w}|\,h=|\vec{v}\times\vec{w}|\,|\vec{u}|\,|\cos\varphi|=|\vec{u}\cdot(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})|.
$$
{{End hidden}}

== Properties ==

=== invariance under cyclic permutation ===

$$
\vec{u}\cdot(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})=\vec{w}\cdot(\vec{u}\times\vec{v})=\vec{v}\cdot(\vec{w}\times\vec{u})
$$

<blockquote>
Intuition: [[#geometrical interpretation|The parallelepiped spanned by three vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$]] is unique.
</blockquote>

=== Vanishing under coplanarity ===

$$
\vec{u}\cdot(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})=0
\iff
\vec{u},\vec{v},\vec{w}\text{ coplanar}.
$$

<blockquote>
Intuition: When the three vectors are coplanar, [[#geometrical interpretation|the parallelepiped spanned by them in $\mathbb{R}^3$]] has vanishing volume.
</blockquote>

== Relationship to matrices ==

$$
\vec{u}\cdot(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})
=
\det\begin{pmatrix}
u_1 & u_2 & u_3\\
v_1 & v_2 & v_3\\
w_1 & w_2 & w_3
\end{pmatrix}.
$$
